data.one_liner: Secure key‑value storage for Flutter with platform‑specific backends.
data.what_it_does: Provides encrypted storage on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and web. Supports optional caching for faster reads and a unified API across platforms.
use_when: You need to store secrets or encryption keys securely on the device
You want a single API that works on mobile, desktop and web
You prefer a lightweight plugin over a full‑blown database
avoid_when: You only need plain, non‑encrypted preferences
You require complex relational queries or large data sets
strengths: True platform‑native encryption (Keychain, EncryptedSharedPreferences, wincred, Secret Service)
weaknesses: Requires native setup per platform (e.g., Keychain sharing, backup exclusions)
No built‑in migration or versioning tools
data.setup_notes: Add platform‑specific configuration: enable Keychain Sharing on iOS/macOS, disable Auto Backup or add backup rules on Android, ensure Secret Service is running on Linux, no extra steps for web beyond providing password and salt.

alternatives.name: flutter_secure_storage
alternatives.why_pick_it: Mature plugin with similar secure storage features and broader community support

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: Simpler API for non‑secure key‑value storage

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: When you need relational queries or larger data sets
